Kindly guide us. 3868 views Q. Ibn Arabi said, "العبد رب و الرب عبد" or "al-`abd-u rabb-un wa-r-rabb-u `abd-un" (the slave is the lord and the lord is the slave)." Sufis claim that such statements were always considered to be the most elevated exposition of mystical thought in Islam, and therefore unsuitable for the untrained mind. Ibn Arabi has also said, "الرب رب في التنزل والعبد عبد في الترقى" or "ar-rabb-u rabb-un f? t-tanazzul-i wa-l-`abd-u `abd-un f? t-taraqq?" answer: Miscellaneous >> Tasawwuf Question ID: 30262 Country: United Kingdom Title: I would be extremely appreciative if you could take the time to inform me of the Deobandi stance on the Hadra Zikr of Sufis; moreover of it's legal status and the reasoning behind this? Question: As salamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuh, I would be extremely appreciative if you could take the time to inform me of the Deobandi stance on the Hadra Zikr of Sufis; moreover of it's legal status and the reasoning behind this? Wasalaam, Usmaan. Answer ID: 30262 Posted on: Sep 1, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 387/387/M=1432) If you intend to know Shariah ruling about loud Zikr, you should know that it is alright in some cases without any karahat while in some cases it is makrooh. Those who allow loud Zikr it is for treatment, it strokes heart and causes warmth that is useful in this chain. فالإسرار أفضل حيث خيف الرياء أو تأذي المصلين أو النيام ، والجهر أفضل حيث خلا مما ذكر لأنه أكثر عملاً ولتعدي فائدته إلى السامعين ، ويوقظ قلب الذاكر الخ (شامى) Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
